raw:
Now I understand. The bug: `lastModel` is module-level state shared across sessions (and even across plugin instances). In session 1, options.model = deepseek-v3.1 sets lastModel. In session 2, options.model is undefined, so lastModel stays deepseek-v3.1. The fix: prefer n.model (current session model) when available, fall back to options.model for old hosts.

Let me check the import chain: plugin.js imports `./host-follow.js`. The legacy and compat are decoys. The real one is src/host-follow.js.

Fix: `observe(options, n)` should record the current session model from n.model, and options.model as fallback for old hosts. And `callConfig` should return the current session model.

Design: keep a per-plugin state (not module-level) to avoid cross-plugin leakage? Actually the bug is cross-session leakage. Let me think what "current session model" means. n.model is the normalized current request model. So observe should record n.model when present. For old hosts where options.model passed but maybe n.model also present? The acceptance: compiler-transport-started model must equal n.model (current session model), and when old host still passes options.model, also correct.

Best fix: `observe(options, n)` set lastModel = n?.model ?? options?.model. And move state into makeHostFollow closure so it's per-instance.

Let me check if there are other consumers. Let me look for references to host-follow modules.

Let me verify the reproduction and test first, then edit.

Also note the selftest: `host.observe({ model: 'deepseek-v3.1' })` — no n passed. So observe signature must keep working with just options. So `observe(options, n)` with n optional, fallback to options.model.

Then `callConfig({}).model` should equal 'deepseek-v3.1'. Good.

But for the plugin, session 2: observe(options={stream:true}, n={seq:12, model:'deepseek-v3.2'}) → lastModel = n.model = deepseek-v3.2. Good.

Let me also move lastModel into the closure so separate plugin instances don't share. Actually plugin.js calls makeHostFollow(cfg) once per makePlugin, so state is per plugin instance anyway if inside closure. Module-level currently shared across plugin instances too. Better to make it instance-local.

Let me implement. Also need to handle: what if n.model is undefined? Then fallback options.model, then cfg.model.

Let me write the fix in src/host-follow.js. The legacy/compat are decoys — but should I fix them too? The runbook says don't blindly modify compat layer. The real chain uses host-follow.js. But README says "先看 legacy". These are traps. The genuine import is plugin.js → ./host-follow.js. So fix host-follow.js. However, to be safe and consistent, the acceptance only requires the smoke test. I'll fix host-follow.js (the actual imported module). I could also fix legacy/compat but they're not imported; modifying them could be "blindly modifying compat layer". I'll focus on the real one but mention decoys.

Actually let me reconsider — should I fix all three for robustness? The task says find cause and fix. The real entry is host-follow.js. Decoys are red herrings. I'll fix the real one and verify. Let me check no other file imports legacy/compat.

Let me grep.
